reason: The finding holds; it is a measurement step only, so no LB, private or R1-R10 risk. Checked in code: (a) lb_poll.py runs `while True` at module level, so importing it starts a second poller. (b) The poller stamps ts before poll(); runtime_ledger.py adds 210 s only per failed attempt (l.91-92, l.193), accepts any header suffix (l.74) and sorts polls by ts (l.135). The manual polls are pivotal. The poller cadence is 601.6 s (02:13:16 to 03:23:27 over 7 cycles), so the projected polls are ~07:54:09Z and ~08:04:11Z. The forecast F(K2) = 7.87 h puts the K2 finish at ~07:54:24Z, which falls inside that gap. Without the manual polls, A5-L(K2) would read POSSIBLE, not CLEAN, for most outcomes near the forecast. That affects READ TABLE rows 4/5 and the D4/deadline ask to the user. The plan is cheap: 2 read-only CLI calls, no poller restart, no writes except appends to poll.log in the parsed format. It is also harmless if K2 has already finished, because the ledger breaks at the first result. One defect in the script as given: stamping AFTER the call also stamps PENDING observations late. A5-L is FIRED when the last PENDING poll is later than 8.0 h (lo_h > 8.0; the 8.0 h mark is 08:02:12Z). With timeout=100 s, a call that starts at 08:00:45-08:00:50 and returns PENDING after 08:02:12 would fire A5-L spuriously and trigger a false D4/deadline question to the user. A second, smaller point: the relative LOG path depends on the working directory.
fix: Run the script as proposed, but with 3 changes. (1) Set timeout=75 on the 08:00:45 call, which is safe for both states: 08:00:50 + 75 s < 08:02:12. (2) Use an absolute path for LOG (C:/Users/vital/Documents/kAGGLE/Biohub - Cell Tracking During Development/experiments/lb_poll/poll.log). (3) Optionally add a third one-shot at 08:01:45Z with timeout=20. It shrinks the unprovable window from 08:00:4x-08:02:12 to 08:01:4x-08:02:12. Keep the rest: skip the write on empty stdout or an exception, use the header '=== ts [manual one-shot, stamped after call]', keep the first 60 lines, never import lb_poll, never restart the poller. Start the script once with run_in_background; it has the same lifetime dependency on the main session as the poller (PID started 02:12:45). After 08:02Z run `python tools/runtime_ledger.py --print` once and read A5-L(K2). Only CLEAR proves d1 is clean.
realistic_gain: 0 LB points (measurement only). It turns a likely A5-L POSSIBLE (not clean) into a provable CLEAR when K2 finishes between ~07:54:09Z and the last manual poll. That is the forecast finish (07:54:24Z), so the probability that this matters is high. It decides READ TABLE row 4 vs row 5 if d1 <= -0.002, and it avoids a spurious runtime-trigger question to the user. The cost is 2-3 read-only API calls.
